items.title: Technology-enabled personalized nutrition interventions for adolescents with type 1 diabetes: a systematic review
items.venue: Journal of Health Population and Nutrition

ai.headline: Digital tools that personalise nutrition advice may help teenagers with type 1 diabetes manage blood sugar and feel less burdened.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 35 studies involving over 1,500 adolescents aged 10–25 with type 1 diabetes looked at technology-based personalised nutrition interventions. It found that fat-and-protein-aware bolus calculators, AI-driven dietary assessment tools, simplified meal announcement strategies in automated insulin delivery systems, and gamified feedback apps were linked to better glucose control, more accurate carbohydrate counting, and lower psychosocial burden.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday digital tools could make managing type 1 diabetes less stressful and more accurate for young people.
ai.life_skill: Try using a diabetes app that gives real-time feedback and personalised meal suggestions if you are managing type 1 diabetes, and discuss it with your diabetes care team.
ai.fact: Personalised digital nutrition tools were linked to improvements in blood sugar control and reduced diabetes-related stress in adolescents with type 1 diabetes.

quiz.question: What did the review find about simplified meal announcement strategies in automated insulin delivery systems?
quiz.answer: They were non-inferior to precise carbohydrate counting for time in range and reduced cognitive burden, though some increase in prolonged hyperglycemia was observed.

ai.caveat: The review includes many non-randomised and qualitative studies, so the findings show links rather than proof that the technologies caused the improvements.

items.title: Effectiveness of eHealth lifestyle interventions on management of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

ai.headline: Digital lifestyle programmes can help adults with fatty liver disease lose weight and improve liver health.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 28 trials involving 2,579 adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. eHealth lifestyle programmes—using goal setting, education, monitoring, feedback and reminders—were linked to greater weight loss, lower liver enzyme levels and better self-management than standard care.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that phone- or computer-based support may be a practical way for people with fatty liver disease to manage their health alongside usual care.
ai.life_skill: Try using a reputable health app or online programme to set goals, track food and activity, and get feedback if you are managing fatty liver disease.
ai.fact: eHealth lifestyle interventions were significantly superior to standard care in reducing weight, BMI, waist circumference and liver enzyme levels in adults with MASLD.

quiz.question: What did the review find about eHealth lifestyle programmes compared with standard care for adults with fatty liver disease?
quiz.answer: They were linked to greater reductions in weight, BMI, waist circumference and liver enzyme levels, plus better self-management and quality of life.

ai.caveat: The review included both randomised and non-randomised trials, and the abstract does not report how large the benefits were or how confident the authors were in the evidence.

items.title: Museum-based activities and psychological wellbeing: a pre–post study of visual thinking strategies and guided visits across two cultural settings

ai.headline: Two short museum activities were linked to lower anxiety and better mood in adults.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 135 adults who took part in either a visual thinking strategies session or a standard guided visit at two museums in Milan. Both activities were followed by short-term reductions in state anxiety and improvements in mood, with no clear difference between the two activities.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that brief, non-therapeutic museum visits may be a simple way to support everyday wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Try visiting a museum or gallery and notice how you feel before and after.
ai.fact: Both visual thinking strategies and standard guided visits were linked to similar short-term improvements in state anxiety and mood.

quiz.question: Did the study find that one museum activity worked better than the other for reducing anxiety?
quiz.answer: No, there was no statistically detectable difference between the visual thinking strategies session and the standard guided visit.

ai.caveat: This was a pre–post study without a control group or randomisation, so the improvements cannot be causally attributed to the museum activities.

items.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt

ai.headline: A soy compound protected mice from salt-related harm to blood pressure, memory and social behaviour.
ai.summary: Japanese researchers studied mice fed a high-salt diet and tested a soy-derived compound called LPC70. Mice given LPC70 had lower blood pressure, better memory and improved social interactions than mice on excess salt alone.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that too much salt may affect the brain as well as blood pressure, and that a natural compound might one day help counteract some of those effects.

quiz.question: What did mice given LPC70 show compared with mice on excess salt alone?
quiz.answer: They had lower blood pressure, better memory and improved social interactions.

ai.caveat: The findings are from mice, so they may not apply to humans.

items.title: AI feedback does not motivate by itself: a motivational-meaning model for university physical education

ai.headline: AI feedback in PE only motivates if learners understand and accept its meaning, not because it is technically precise.
ai.summary: The paper proposes a motivational-meaning model for university physical education, drawing on self-determination theory, feedback literacy, self-regulated learning and motor-learning research. It argues that how AI feedback is framed, made socially visible, and checked against bodily experience shapes whether learners see it as informational or controlling, which then affects psychological needs such as autonomy and competence. The model offers testable design principles rather than evidence that AI feedback improves learning or participation.
ai.why_it_matters: It reminds us that digital feedback tools do not automatically motivate people; the way feedback is presented and interpreted matters just as much as the technology itself.
ai.life_skill: Notice how feedback makes you feel and whether it helps you decide your own next step, rather than assuming it is useful just because it comes from AI.
ai.fact: The paper distinguishes informational meaning from controlling meaning in feedback and links them to subsequent psychological-need experiences.

quiz.question: Does the paper claim that AI feedback automatically improves learning or participation?
quiz.answer: No, it offers testable design principles rather than evidence that AI feedback improves learning or participation.

ai.caveat: The paper presents a theoretical model with propositions, not tested evidence from a study.

items.title: Upgrading Financial Markets -- by Francis Annan, Seth Garz

ai.headline: Holding financial agents accountable improves services and boosts savings and incomes more than access alone.
ai.summary: Researchers tested upgrading village savings groups into mobile money and bank agents across 195 rural Sierra Leonean communities, with some also receiving a monthly consumer feedback mechanism. Upgrading expanded access, but feedback drove large operational improvements, especially in privacy and consumer protection, leading to higher usage, revenues, savings digitisation and incomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that making financial providers answerable to customers can matter as much as simply building more access points.
ai.life_skill: Ask for and use feedback channels when using financial services so providers stay accountable to you.
ai.fact: In the study, communities with upgraded savings groups plus monthly consumer feedback saw large improvements in privacy and consumer protection, along with higher usage and incomes.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find mattered most for improving financial services in rural Sierra Leone?
quiz.answer: Adding a monthly consumer feedback mechanism to upgraded village savings groups drove large operational improvements and higher usage and incomes.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability

ai.headline: A new AI framework builds subjective mental worlds to predict thoughts and behavior more accurately than current language models.
ai.summary: The paper introduces the Mental World Model and its Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture, which construct subjective worlds and simulate how mental states evolve over time. On two theory-of-mind benchmarks, MMEA achieved 96.48% and 94.00% accuracy, outperforming leading LLMs and specialized methods.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible path toward AI that understands people’s underlying mental states rather than just surface-level language.
ai.life_skill: Notice how someone’s past experiences might shape their current reactions, not just their words.
ai.fact: MMEA scored 96.48% on DynToM and 94.00% on RecToM benchmarks.

quiz.question: What did MMEA outperform on the DynToM and RecToM benchmarks?
quiz.answer: It outperformed leading large language models and specialized Theory of Mind methods.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet independently confirmed.

items.title: Unpacking the Effect of Classroom Social Environment on Self-Regulated Learning in Mathematical Education: The Mediation of Self-Efficacy

ai.headline: Supportive classrooms and self-belief help students manage their own maths learning.
ai.summary: The study looked at 1,640 Chinese elementary and secondary students and four classroom social factors: teacher emotional support, teacher academic support, student cooperation, and student cohesiveness. Student cooperation and teacher academic support were the strongest direct predictors of self-regulated learning in maths, while self-belief (self-efficacy) helped link classroom support to better self-regulated learning.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how students feel supported in class can shape the way they take charge of their own learning.
ai.life_skill: Notice which classroom habits or teacher support help you feel more confident tackling maths on your own.
ai.fact: Self-efficacy acted as a significant mediator between classroom social environment factors and self-regulated learning in mathematics.

quiz.question: Which two classroom factors were the strongest direct predictors of self-regulated learning in maths?
quiz.answer: Student cooperation and teacher academic support were the strongest direct predictors.

ai.caveat: The study used data from students in China at one point in time, so it cannot prove that classroom support causes better self-regulated learning.

items.title: Protecting workers from increasing heat
authors: Maysaa Nemer, Vidhya Venugopal, Anna Suraya, Farzana Misha

ai.headline: Heat exposure harms billions of workers worldwide, causing injuries, deaths, and lost income.
ai.summary: The paper reviews evidence on hazardous heat at work. It finds that 2.41 billion workers are exposed to excessive heat each year, linked to 22.85 million injuries and 18,970 deaths, while a meta-analysis found 35% of heat-exposed workers experienced heat strain and 30% reported productivity losses.
ai.why_it_matters: Rising heat from climate change is making work more dangerous and costly, especially for people with the least protection.
ai.life_skill: Notice heat, humidity, workload, shade, water, and rest breaks when working in hot conditions.
ai.fact: In 2024, heat caused an estimated 639 billion lost working hours and $1.09tn in lost income.

quiz.question: What share of heat-exposed workers experienced heat strain in the meta-analysis?
quiz.answer: 35% of workers exposed to heat experienced heat strain.

ai.caveat: This is a commentary drawing on multiple sources rather than a single new study, so the figures come from the cited research rather than original analysis.

items.title: Comorbidity Exposure-Window Definitions and Multidimensional Disparities in Long COVID Risk: Evidence from a U.S. National Cohort (2020-2024)

ai.headline: How researchers define pre-existing health conditions changes long COVID risk estimates by up to 314%.
ai.summary: Researchers studied over 6 million U.S. adults with COVID-19 to see how different ways of counting pre-existing health conditions affect long COVID risk. They found that counting conditions before infection rather than before long COVID diagnosis produced much higher risk estimates, and that risks fell over time while disparities remained.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how health data is measured can change our understanding of who is at risk and how prevention should be targeted.
ai.life_skill: Check how a health study measured pre-existing conditions before accepting its risk figures.
ai.fact: Long COVID risk estimates varied widely depending on whether comorbidities were recorded before infection or before diagnosis.

quiz.question: What happened to long COVID risk estimates when comorbidities were defined before infection instead of before diagnosis?
quiz.answer: They yielded 8%-314% higher adjusted attributable risks and 3%-34% higher adjusted relative risks across 16 major comorbidities.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Cognitive tests of pattern separation as sleep-sensitive measures in middle-aged and older adults: An exploratory study

ai.headline: Better sleep quantity is linked to better pattern separation test performance in adults aged 50 and over.
ai.summary: Researchers monitored sleep for seven days in 34 adults aged 50 or older using wrist actigraphy and sleep diaries, then tested their cognition. They found that objective sleep quantity was linked to performance on a pattern separation test and a vigilance test, and predicted pattern separation performance after accounting for age, sex and education.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that sleep may affect a type of memory linked to early dementia, though this small preprint cannot prove cause and effect.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your memory for similar details feels worse after a poor night’s sleep.
ai.fact: Pattern separation is the ability to distinguish between similar experiences or memories.

quiz.question: What did the study find about sleep quantity and pattern separation tests?
quiz.answer: Objective sleep quantity was linked to pattern separation test performance and predicted it after controlling for age, sex and education.

ai.caveat: This is a small, exploratory preprint with 34 participants, not yet peer reviewed, so it cannot show that sleep causes changes in memory.

items.title: Exercise therapy for temporomandibular disorders.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: A Cochrane review will assess whether exercise therapy helps adults with jaw disorders.
ai.summary: This is a protocol for a planned Cochrane systematic review. It aims to assess the effects of exercise therapy on pain intensity, jaw function or disability, and health-related quality of life in adults with temporomandibular disorders, compared with no treatment, placebo, or other non-exercise conservative interventions.
ai.why_it_matters: It will help people understand whether exercise therapy is a useful option for managing jaw pain and disability.
ai.caveat: This is only a review protocol; no results or findings are available yet.

items.title: The case for AI degrowth

ai.headline: The paper argues that current AI development is incompatible with a sustainable economy and calls for limits on AI growth.
ai.summary: This is a commentary article that argues AI, as it currently develops, relies on fossil energy and competitive growth, making it incompatible with economic degrowth and sustainability.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a perspective on how technology choices may affect the environment and the future of the economy.
ai.life_skill: Notice how the digital tools you use depend on energy and resources.
ai.fact: The article frames AI growth as linked to fossil energy use and enclosed commons.

quiz.question: What does the paper say about limits to AI growth?
quiz.answer: The paper says limits to AI growth are not technophobia but a chance for a liveable future.

ai.caveat: This is a single opinion piece, not a study with data, so it does not prove that AI causes environmental harm.

items.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report

ai.headline: A new AI model can link its answers to specific parts of an image, improving how it understands visual regions.
ai.summary: Researchers developed Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4-billion-parameter multimodal AI model, to improve fine-grained region understanding in images. It predicts masks from its own visual representations and outperformed its base model across referring comprehension and perception benchmarks.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows how AI systems are getting better at connecting language to specific visual details, which could make image-based tools more useful in daily life.
ai.life_skill: Try checking whether an AI tool can point to the exact part of an image it is describing before trusting its answer.
ai.fact: Xiaomi-Lens-0 gained 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 across eight referring comprehension splits.

quiz.question: What did Xiaomi-Lens-0 predict from its own visual representations?
quiz.answer: It predicted masks from its own visual representations.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet independently confirmed.

items.title: Could staying active before surgery help prevent postoperative delirium?

ai.headline: Being active before cancer surgery may be linked to a lower risk of postoperative delirium.
ai.summary: Researchers looked at physical activity before cancer surgery and its link to postoperative delirium. People who were active at least seven times a week before surgery were linked to a lower risk of developing delirium after surgery.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests everyday physical activity might help protect the brain around the time of surgery.
ai.life_skill: Try to stay regularly active in the weeks before planned surgery, if your health allows.
ai.fact: Regular physical activity before cancer surgery was linked to a lower risk of postoperative delirium.

quiz.question: What was physical activity before cancer surgery linked to in the research?
quiz.answer: It was linked to a lower risk of developing postoperative delirium.

ai.caveat: This is a news report of research presented at a meeting, not a peer-reviewed study, so the findings are preliminary and not proof.

items.title: Scaling Up: A Multi-Site Trial of e-SBI for Alcohol Use in Pregnancy

ai.headline: A trial is testing whether a phone app helps pregnant women cut down alcohol use.
ai.summary: The study looks at whether pregnant women who screen positive for alcohol risk like using the MommyCheckup app, a technology-delivered brief intervention, and whether it reduces their alcohol use. It also tests whether booster sessions and tailored text messages make the app work better.
ai.why_it_matters: It could show whether easy-to-use digital tools can support healthier choices during pregnancy and reduce risks to babies.
ai.life_skill: Try looking for trusted digital health tools if you want support cutting down alcohol during pregnancy, and discuss options with a midwife or doctor.
ai.fact: Alcohol use in pregnancy is linked to fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.

quiz.question: What is the app in the study called?
quiz.answer: It is called MommyCheckup.

ai.caveat: This is a trial record with results posted, not a full peer-reviewed paper, so the findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be

ai.headline: Neuroscience evidence suggests that intelligence alone is not enough for AI to have subjective experience.
ai.summary: This commentary argues that while large language models can mimic thought and feeling, they lack the biological basis for consciousness. It states that evidence from neuroscience indicates intelligence is distinct from subjective experience.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps you understand that AI systems are sophisticated tools, not sentient beings, which changes how you interpret their responses and interactions.
ai.life_skill: Notice that AI can mimic emotions without actually feeling them, so do not assume it has personal experiences or intentions.
ai.fact: Intelligence and subjective experience are distinct concepts, and having one does not guarantee the other.

quiz.question: According to the abstract, why is intelligence alone not sufficient for consciousness?
quiz.answer: Because evidence from neuroscience suggests that intelligence and subjective experience are separate things.

ai.caveat: This is a commentary piece arguing a theoretical point based on existing neuroscience, not a new experimental study proving AI lacks consciousness.

items.title: Factoring daily weather extremes into glacier models reveals greater ice loss and faster sea-level rise

ai.headline: Including daily weather extremes in models suggests glaciers will lose ice faster than previously thought.
ai.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and Vrije Universiteit Brussel improved glacier models by accounting for daily weather variability, such as heat waves. This approach resulted in simulations showing greater projected ice loss by the end of the century compared to previous estimates.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding that short-lived extreme weather events significantly accelerate ice loss helps explain why sea-level rise projections may need to be updated.
ai.life_skill: Notice that short-term weather events can have long-term cumulative effects on large-scale systems like glaciers.
ai.fact: Accounting for daily weather variability in glacier models leads to more realistic simulations of melt and higher projected ice loss.

quiz.question: How did including daily weather extremes change the projected ice loss?
quiz.answer: It resulted in greater projected ice loss by the end of the century.

ai.caveat: These findings are based on computer simulations and models, not direct long-term observations of all glaciers.

items.title: Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy

ai.headline: Baseline molecular features may predict treatment response in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed genomic, transcriptomic and epigenetic samples from patients newly diagnosed with multiple myeloma who received quadruplet induction therapy followed by MRD-guided consolidation. Baseline molecular features were associated with minimal residual disease status after induction.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how molecular profiling could help doctors understand who is likely to respond to treatment in a serious blood cancer.
ai.fact: Baseline genomic, transcriptomic and epigenetic features are associated with MRD status after induction in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy.

quiz.question: What were baseline molecular features associated with after induction therapy?
quiz.answer: They were associated with minimal residual disease status.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study, so it shows a link rather than proof that the molecular features predict outcomes.

items.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia
authors: Camilo Sanz, Santiago Martínez Medina, Scott D Stonington

ai.headline: A man in Colombia faced long delays before a gastric cancer diagnosis was made.
ai.summary: The paper describes Pepe, a 45-year-old self-employed hauler in Cali, Colombia. After months of abdominal heaviness and burning, he was initially treated for reflux disease; a gastroscopy two months later revealed an ulcerated mass.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how delays in getting diagnostic tests can affect people with serious symptoms.
ai.life_skill: If symptoms persist or worsen despite initial treatment, follow up with a healthcare professional.
ai.fact: Gastroscopy can reveal an ulcerated mass in the stomach.

quiz.question: What did the gastroscopy reveal in Pepe?
quiz.answer: It revealed an ulcerated mass.

ai.caveat: This is a single patient perspective, not evidence about how common delays are or what causes them.

items.title: Scientists link a strange sugar in red meat to a 63% higher diabetes risk

ai.headline: People who ate the most of a sugar in red meat had a 63% higher risk of type 2 diabetes.
ai.summary: Researchers studied nearly 90,000 adults and found that those consuming the most of a little-known sugar found in red meat had a 63% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Scientists suspect the sugar may trigger chronic inflammation, suggesting a link between red meat and diabetes beyond weight gain.
ai.why_it_matters: This could help explain why eating lots of red meat is linked to type 2 diabetes, beyond just weight gain.
ai.life_skill: Try eating red meat less often and choosing other protein sources such as beans, fish or poultry.
ai.fact: A little-known sugar found in red meat may be linked to chronic inflammation and type 2 diabetes risk.

quiz.question: What did the study link to a higher risk of type 2 diabetes?
quiz.answer: People who consumed the most of a little-known sugar found in red meat had a 63% higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

ai.caveat: This was an observational study, so it shows a link but cannot prove the sugar causes diabetes.

items.title: Why Shared-Savings ACOs Have Failed to Deliver for Primary Care
authors: Lisa S. Rotenstein Nicholas Stine and Bruce Landon

ai.headline: Shared-Savings ACOs fail primary care
ai.summary: Researchers studied Shared-Savings ACOs and their impact on primary care. They found that these ACOs have failed to deliver for primary care. The study examined the effectiveness of Shared-Savings ACOs in improving primary care outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it affects the quality and accessibility of primary care for patients
ai.life_skill: Check with your healthcare provider about the type of care model they use
ai.fact: Shared-Savings ACOs have not improved primary care as intended

quiz.answer: Shared-Savings ACOs

items.title: El Niño is dramatically increasing sea levels – how bad could it get?

ai.headline: El Niño raises sea levels
ai.summary: Researchers studied the impact of El Niño on sea levels, finding a significant increase in the eastern Pacific, and warning of potential coastal flooding. El Niño has already raised sea levels in part of the eastern Pacific. The strengthening of El Niño could lead to coastal flooding from Alaska to Chile.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters to everyday life as it could lead to coastal flooding and affect communities living in these areas.
ai.life_skill: Check news for weather warnings in your area
ai.fact: El Niño is linked to increased sea levels in the eastern Pacific

quiz.answer: Sea levels are increasing, already by 40 centimetres in part of the eastern Pacific.

ai.summary: Researchers reviewed studies on social media and AI in Indian agricultural communication, finding recent and descriptive evidence. items.title: A systematic review on the challenges facing Latin-American tropical dairy cattle production.

ai.headline: Tropical dairy farming faces challenges
ai.summary: Researchers studied the challenges facing Latin-American tropical dairy cattle production, finding that heat stress, feed scarcity, and disease pressure impair animal performance. The study highlights the need for sustainable planning and integrated strategies to address these challenges. Tropical dairy systems face environmental, nutritional, health, economic, and social constraints that can reduce productivity and product quality.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because the demand for dairy products is expected to surge in developing countries, particularly in tropical regions, and sustainable production is crucial for food security and ecosystem protection.
ai.life_skill: Try to support sustainable farming practices in your daily choices
ai.fact: Tropical livestock farming dominates the global scene in terms of the number of animals, output, and stakeholders

quiz.question: What is a major challenge facing tropical dairy cattle production?
quiz.answer: Heat stress, feed scarcity, and disease pressure are major challenges facing tropical dairy cattle production

items.title: Mental health interventions for adolescents with depression and anxiety in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review of the evidence

ai.headline: Non-specialist-led programmes may help reduce depression symptoms in adolescents in lower-income countries.
ai.summary: A systematic review looked at 22 trials involving 2,336 adolescents across 11 low- and middle-income countries. It found high-certainty evidence that interventions delivered by non-specialists may reduce depression symptoms, but could not say whether school-based or non-school-based settings were better, nor whether non-specialists help with anxiety.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how communities with few mental health professionals might still support young people’s wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you or a friend feel persistently low or anxious, and speak to a trusted adult or a qualified mental health professional about getting support.
ai.fact: Anxiety and depression make up about 40% of mental disorders in adolescents aged 10 to 19 worldwide.

quiz.question: What did the review find about non-specialist-delivered interventions for adolescent depression?
quiz.answer: They showed potential effectiveness for reducing depression symptoms with high certainty.

ai.caveat: The review included only 22 trials and the evidence was insufficient to determine effects on anxiety or whether school-based settings are better.

items.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood

ai.headline: A small study found blueberries may reduce depressive symptoms in older adults, but the benefit was not statistically significant versus placebo.
ai.summary: Researchers studied older adults who ate blueberries every day for three months and found greater reductions in depressive symptoms than those taking a placebo. They also saw changes in gut microbial enzymes, hinting at a possible gut-brain link. However, the mood improvement was not statistically significant compared with placebo.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how diet might be linked to mood through the gut, but the evidence is too weak to rely on blueberries alone for mental health.
ai.life_skill: Try eating a variety of fruits, including blueberries, as part of a balanced diet while looking after your mental wellbeing.
ai.fact: The study found changes in gut microbial enzymes among older adults eating blueberries daily for three months.

quiz.question: Were the mood benefits of eating blueberries statistically significant compared with placebo?
quiz.answer: No, the mood benefits were not statistically significant compared with placebo.

ai.caveat: The study was small and the mood benefits were not statistically significant compared with placebo, so the results are not proof that blueberries improve mood.

items.title: Modelling of a consumer basket in food retail trade taking into account nutritional criteria

ai.headline: A model suggests taxing unhealthy food could cut demand and fund healthier eating programmes.
ai.summary: The study used economic modelling and official data from Ukraine to look at food consumption and nutrition.
